title: Second-Order DPA Beyond Hamming-Weight Leakage
summary: For Pearson-correlation second-order DPA, optimal-model and normalized-product conclusions rely on Hamming-weight leakage; their counterparts for other leakage functions remain open.

formal_statement.body: In Pearson-correlation-based second-order differential power analysis, conclusions about the optimal prediction model and the optimal way to combine leakage samples, including the assessment that the normalized-product combination is the best analyzed choice, were obtained under a fixed Hamming-weight leakage function. Determine how replacing Hamming weight with another leakage function affects those conclusions: characterize the resulting optimal prediction model and sample-combination function, and establish whether the normalized product remains optimal.

scope.domain: Side-channel cryptanalysis using Pearson-correlation-based second-order differential power analysis.
assumptions: Pearson's correlation coefficient is used to evaluate second-order differential power analysis.
The existing optimality conclusions assume a fixed Hamming-weight leakage function.
parameters: Leakage function: varied from Hamming weight to another leakage function
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize the optimal prediction model and leakage-sample combination function for other leakage functions, and determine whether the normalized product remains optimal.

citations.label: The World Is Not Enough: Another Look on Second-Order DPA

progress.summary: The source says prior observations about optimal prediction and leakage-sample combination were derived for a fixed Hamming-weight leakage function. It explicitly leaves their behavior under a different leakage function open.
citation_labels: François-Xavier Standaert et al., The World Is Not Enough: Another Look on Second-Order DPA
